Specification of Diagnostics
AUTOSAR AP R25-11
The nature of data stored and retrieved via
extended data records
is typical of
standard scalar data types. Mostly
extended data records
represent counters or
comparable statistic data related to a DTC. While a
snapshot record
could contain
complexer data information at the time a fault was detected, the
extended data
record
is simpler. This is reflected also within the interface.
The typed and generated
extendend-data-record-element-interface-
name-x
class has an interface that is designed to meet the purpose providing these
simple data information from an application.
The main difference to UDS
DiagnosticDataElement read operation
is, that
extended data record data shall always be available and no NRC as return value is
supported. There are no known use cases for applications returning extended data to
not provide data to the read request. Dedicated invalid value information, such as the
use of 0xFF for
invalid
can be used, if this is needed. Especially the UDS protocol has
no means to omit data in the positive response stream. A UDS client relies, that data
positions are kept in the response, especially if multiple data elements are part of the
response. Here data elements with no value cannot be serialized to the UDS response
message.
[SWS_DM_00895] Triggering for extended data record storage and updates
Upstream requirements:
RS_Diag_04206, RS_Diag_04127
⌈
The data collection and storage of the
extended data record
shall be trig-
gered by the
DiagnosticExtendedDataRecord.trigger
. Updating extended
data records after being first stored, shall be configurable with the
DiagnosticEx-
tendedDataRecord.update
configuration parameter. The data layout of
extended
data record
is defined by the order of
DiagnosticExtendedDataRecord.ele-
ment
. Each
DiagnosticExtendedDataRecordElement
shall be captured in its
order via the corresponding read function instance for typed ExtendedDataRecordEle-
